item.title: Int'l counter-terrorism forum opens in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Over 320 representatives from 62 countries and international organizations have gathered in Beijing for the three-day Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counter-Terrorism. Hosted by the Chinese People's Armed Police Force, this year's forum provides a platform for representatives to share insights and experience on pragmatic cooperation in the fight against terrorism in four seminar sessions. Topics such as trends of terrorist activities facilitated by unmanned weapons and intelligent technology, and corresponding counter-terrorism capacity building, are on the agenda for discussion. Visits to military training demonstrations and viewing of unmanned equipment have also been scheduled for the attendees, the organizer of the forum said. The armed police form an important force for a country in combating terrorism and safeguarding social stability. The Chinese People's Armed Police Force has hosted five editions of this forum since 2016, with the aim of pooling global strengths to erect an impregnable fortress against terrorism. An important participant in and contributor to the global fight against terrorism, China has conducted pragmatic cooperation with other countries in terms of intelligence exchanges, border control, case investigations and counter-terrorism financing. The country has also organized training sessions and seminars to share its experience with the international community and help with capacity building in combating terrorism.

item.title: Xi calls for decisive progress in Healthy China advancement
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech during a national meeting on health in Beijing, capital of China. The meeting was held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has called for efforts to firmly follow a path with Chinese characteristics in developing the country's health programs, to secure decisive progress in the Healthy China Initiative over the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a national meeting on health held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. Xi stressed that people's health is a key benchmark of a nation's prosperity and strength. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the Party has made a major decision to launch the Healthy China Initiative, promoting the establishment of the world's largest systems of medical services, traditional medicine, disease prevention and control, and healthcare security, said Xi, noting that the country has achieved historic accomplishments and made all-round progress in healthcare. In 2025, China's average life expectancy rose to 79.25 years, while its major health indicators remained at the leading position among upper-middle-income countries and countries with a population exceeding 100 million. Xi said the goal is to build a Healthy China, where health services are ensured in a balanced, inclusive, high-quality and efficient manner. Xi stressed that people's health should be factored into all policies and reflected in every aspect of work. Prevention, he said, is the most cost-effective and efficient approach to protecting public health. He called for greater emphasis on foundational health work, addressing risks at their source, and encouraging the public to adopt a sound understanding of health and take an active role in managing their own well-being. He also called for a stronger disease prevention and control system to guard against large-scale outbreaks. Xi underscored the need to optimize the functions and structural layout of medical institutions so that people can access medical care close to home and receive effective treatment. China has supported the development of 125 regional medical centers in areas where high-quality medical resources are relatively scarce. Notably, more than 90 percent of residents can access nearby medical and healthcare services within 15 minutes, while primary-level medical institutions account for over 50 percent of all medical visits nationwide. He also urged efforts to improve mechanisms for the preservation and innovative development of traditional Chinese medicine, strengthen basic research and original innovation in the health sector, and enhance the patient experience. Xi stressed that coordinating the development and regulation of medical services, medical insurance, and pharmaceuticals should be a key priority in reforming China's medical and healthcare systems. He also called for efforts to train and develop a sufficient number of highly qualified medical professionals. Efforts will also be made to actively promote the building of a global community of health for all, work with other countries to address major challenges in the health sector, and continuously improve the health and well-being of people around the world, he said. Other Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi attended the event. In his concluding remarks, Li Qiang said Xi's important speech provided guidance for advancing China's health sector. Li called for better coordination between improvements in public health and economic and social development, and urged deeper reform, innovation, opening up and cooperation, stronger prevention and control of major diseases, further development of a tiered diagnosis and treatment system, and greater use of science and technology to improve health services. The meeting was held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi attended the meeting. (Xinhua/Yue Yuewei)

item.title: China says India's publication of Ladakh place names "illegal, void"
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- China has never recognized the so-called "Union Territory of Ladakh" illegally and unilaterally established by India and firmly opposes India's publication of "standard place names in Ladakh," Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Tuesday. Such moves by the Indian side are illegal and null and void, and cannot alter the fact that the western section of the China-India boundary area has always belonged to China, Mao said. She made the remarks in response to a question at Tuesday's press briefing after the government of India said it had identified 28 locations in Ladakh by standard names on an official map.

item.title: Xi, Papua New Guinea's governor-general exchange congratulations over 50th anniversary of diplomatic ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and Bob Dadae, governor-general of Papua New Guinea, on Monday exchanged congratulations on the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. In his message, Xi noted that Papua New Guinea is a good friend, good partner and good brother of China in the Pacific island region. Over the past 50 years since the establishment of diplomatic ties, the two countries have deepened political mutual trust, achieved fruitful results in mutually beneficial cooperation, and expanded people-to-people exchanges, raising bilateral relations to new heights, Xi said. These achievements have benefited the two peoples and injected strong impetus into building a China-Pacific Island countries community with a shared future, said Xi. Noting that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Papua New Guinea relations, Xi said that he stands ready to work with Dadae to take the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations as an opportunity to carry forward traditional friendship, strengthen exchanges and cooperation across various fields, and elevate the comprehensive strategic partnership between China and Papua New Guinea to a new level, so as to deliver greater benefits to the two peoples. For his part, Dadae said that over the past 50 years, bilateral relations have made significant progress, benefiting both countries and their peoples. Papua New Guinea cherishes the longstanding friendship with China, firmly upholds the one-China principle, and looks forward to taking the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations as an opportunity to further deepen and advance bilateral relations, he said. On the same day, Chinese Premier Li Qiang also exchanged congratulations with Papua New Guinea's Prime Minister James Marape. China is willing to work with Papua New Guinea to take the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations as an opportunity to promote high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and advance the comprehensive strategic partnership between China and Papua New Guinea, Li said in the message. For his part, Marape said that the Papua New Guinean government highly appreciates China's significant contributions to the country's economic and social development. Papua New Guinea will continue to uphold the one-China principle it has long adhered to, deepen mutually beneficial cooperation with China across various fields and advance the development of the comprehensive strategic partnership between the two countries, said Marape.

item.title: Chinese foreign ministry slams Taiwan leader's separatist rhetoric
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12
BEIJING, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese mainland and Taiwan belong to one and the same China, and this constitutes the real status quo in the Taiwan Strait, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Monday. Mao made the remarks at a regular news briefing after Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te sought to solicit external support for "Taiwan independence" in a speech in Taipei on Saturday. No matter what Lai says or does, it can't change the historical and legal fact that Taiwan belongs to China, nor can it alter the doomed failure of "Taiwan independence," still less can it stop the overwhelming trend that China will ultimately be reunified, she said. The so-called democracy touted by Lai cannot disguise his separatist agenda, she noted. Taiwan's return to China is an important part of the victorious outcomes of World War II and the post-war international order, the spokesperson said.
